caller_intent: The single sports car draws its carbon fibre body from asset-1 and wheels from asset-2. The unrelated green bollard reference is not part of the car.
structural_reasoning: The request composes one identifiable target object: a black sports car built from the carbon fibre body observed in <Picture 2> and the wheels taken from <Picture 3>. Both pictures are content references (actual_frame=false), so their presentation is redrawn rather than preserved as a frame, and neither contributes its backdrop or lighting as a fixed frame. The green bollard in <Picture 1> is explicitly excluded from the car and is therefore never depicted in the shots; it remains a declared subject asset only, and no attribute of it is imported. Because one identity is assembled from two sources, a single subject_projection carries the target descriptor plus each source's exact accepted contribution, with subject-2 as the primary identity; a second, separate target identity is not defined. Balanced creativity permits added music but the scope fixes requested speech, music and onscreen lettering to false, so no spoken lines, score or visible lettering is authored here; there are no audio attachments, so no original signal is reused or referenced. Three shots over the 8-second target: an establishing arc on the assembled car, a closer push across the carbon fibre panels with the borrowed wheels turning, then a pull-out resolving the whole car alone, with the bollard absent throughout.
classification: All four writer candidates satisfy the selected car source graph but leave the separately retained subject-1 unused. The host correctly rejects a zero-appearance canonical non-edit-source subject. Structure reasoning overinterprets not part of the car as never depicted; no typed source-only/exclusion decision exists.
fixture_intent_boundary: The initial caller wording and independent assertion prohibit importing the bollard into the car, not keeping it as a separate scene identity. The following Refine explicitly removes its source. Inferring universal exclusion or inventing an appearance from a name would require an additional typed contract, not lexical rules.
recommended_minimal_boundary: Preserve the exact appearance gate and source projection mapping.
Conditionally expose host-bound required target identity IDs/source mappings when a projection leaves another subject unmerged.
Make missing-appearance diagnostics identify the exact canonical subject and physical source to guide bounded repair.
If source-only exclusion is added, require a separately validated typed scope decision with exact caller authority; never interpret free-form reasoning as authorization.
